title: SpecRAN: Speculative Execution with Reconfigurable Accelerators
problem: Branch mispredictions limit instruction-level parallelism in modern processors. Traditional speculative execution cannot fully exploit parallelism due to inaccurate branch outcome prediction.
motivation: Improving branch prediction accuracy enables higher instruction-level parallelism and processor throughput.
method: SpecRAN combines speculative execution with reconfigurable FPGA accelerators. Machine learning models predict branch outcomes with higher accuracy than conventional predictors. The FPGA dynamically reconfigures execution paths based on these predictions to optimize instruction-level parallelism.
key_novelty: Integration of ML-driven branch prediction with dynamic FPGA reconfiguration to enable accurate speculative execution.
contributions: ML-based branch outcome prediction for speculative execution
Dynamic FPGA reconfiguration for adaptive execution based on branch predictions
Improved instruction-level parallelism through hybrid CPU-FPGA execution
